headline: Shediac Bay Beach Access and Facilities
reservation: Parlee Beach is a day-use provincial park that generally does not require advance entry permits, though vehicle parking fees apply seasonally. The adjacent Parlee Beach Provincial Park Campground does require advance reservations through the New Brunswick Parks system, particularly for the busy summer months.

days.title: Acadian Shoreline and Sandbars

stops.name: Parlee Beach Waterfront
stops.detail: Walk the supervised sandy stretches known for having some of the warmest saltwater in Canada.

stops.name: Pointe-du-Chêne Wharf
stops.detail: Stroll the historic pier adjacent to the park to watch local fishing boats and coastal activity.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes for local travel; conditions vary with beach traffic.
days.note: Check the daily water quality ratings posted at the park entrance before swimming.

days.title: Shediac Bay Heritage

stops.name: The World's Largest Lobster
stops.detail: Visit this iconic monument in Shediac to learn about the local crustacean industry and regional history.

stops.name: Shediac Bay Island
stops.detail: Observe the protected salt marshes and bird habitats from the shoreline viewpoints.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes from Moncton; conditions vary during peak weekend travel.
days.note: Expect heavy traffic on Route 133 during festival weekends in mid-summer.

days.title: Coastal Estuaries and Trails

stops.name: Scoudouc River Estuary
stops.detail: Explore the calm waters where the river meets the bay, ideal for observing coastal transition zones.

stops.name: Parlee Beach Trail System
stops.detail: Utilize the multi-use paths that connect the campground to the main beach area through wooded sections.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes from Dieppe; conditions vary.
days.note: Biking is a popular way to avoid parking congestion at the main beach gates.

intel.title: Seasonal Day-Use Lots
intel.text: The main paved lot at Parlee Beach is expansive but can reach capacity by noon on hot weekends. Overflow grass lots may be used depending on ground conditions and staff direction.

intel.title: Reliable Coastal Coverage
intel.text: Cellular signal is generally strong throughout the Shediac and Parlee Beach area. Some interference may occur near the wharf during high-occupancy events.

intel.title: Gateway Station Access
intel.text: Full-service stations are located along Main Street in Shediac and at the junction of Highway 15. Ensure you have adequate fuel if planning to tour the rural Acadian coastal roads.

intel.title: Tidal Fluctuations
intel.text: While not as dramatic as the Bay of Fundy, the tides in Shediac Bay affect the width of the beach. Consult local tide tables to maximize sand exposure for walking.

intel.title: Mobility Features
intel.text: Parlee Beach offers specialized beach wheelchairs and accessible boardwalks. Inquire at the park office for current availability and seasonal rental procedures.

plan.arrival: Arrive at Greater Moncton Roméo LeBlanc International Airport (YQM) and take a 20-minute drive northeast to Shediac to pick up beach supplies and local seafood.
plan.vehicle: Standard passenger vehicles are ideal; RVs should use designated parking lanes at the beach to avoid blocking narrow access routes.
plan.goldenHour: The sunset over Shediac Bay from the Pointe-du-Chêne Wharf offers a classic maritime view, depending on seasonal cloud cover.
